summary: Two added comments overstate behavior that the compiler/runtime implementation does not provide.

items.issue: The comment says the compiler calls this when optimizing `Tuple.toArray` on tuples statically known to have at most 22 elements. The optimizer handles the statically known empty tuple separately with `Array.emptyObjectArray`; it calls `productToArray` only for arities 1 through 22.
items.suggestion: Say that the compiler calls it for statically known non-empty tuples of arity at most 22, or remove the optimizer-detail sentence.

items.issue: The summary promises only elements added to the builder, but every factory returns an `ArraySeq` over its full length-`n` array and tracks no final count. Calling `result()` early exposes unfilled default values; adding too many elements fails only through array indexing. The repeated `@param n` claims that exactly `n` elements will be added, but this is not enforced.
items.suggestion: Document `n` as the storage capacity and qualify the result guarantee on compiler-generated callers adding exactly `n` elements, or add bookkeeping/validation that enforces the stated contract.
